sections.label: Small motorised vehicles bills
sections.summary: This Bill and the Active Mobility Bill relate to small motorised vehicles including PMDs and PABs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: This Bill, together with the Active Mobility (Amendment No. 2) Bill, or the "Active Mobility Bill" for short, which will be read next, relates to small motorised vehicles, including personal mobility devices (PMDs) and power-assisted bicycles (PABs).

sections.label: Import control regime
sections.summary: The Small Motorised Vehicles Bill sets out an import control regime to stem inflow of unsafe small motorised vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: The Small Motorised Vehicles (Safety) Bill, or the Small Motorised Vehicles Bill for short, sets out an import control regime to stem the inflow into Singapore of unsafe small motorised vehicles, which include PMDs and PABs.

sections.label: Non-compliant riders detected 2019
sections.summary: In 2019, 972 users were detected riding non-compliant PMDs and PABs on public paths and roads.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: In 2019 alone, 972 users were detected riding non-compliant PMDs and PABs on public paths and public roads.

sections.label: Import approval from LTA
sections.summary: Clause 5 requires all importers to obtain import approval from LTA before bringing small motorised vehicles into Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Clause 5 of the Small Motorised Vehicles Bill requires all importers to obtain import approval from LTA before they can bring small motorised vehicles into Singapore.

sections.label: Offence for misuse of imports
sections.summary: Clause 8 makes it an offence for importers to allow non-compliant devices to be used beyond approved purposes or conditions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: For these specific cases, import approvals can still be granted after LTA has ascertained that these non-compliant devices will not be abused and eventually used on public paths where they could be a danger to other path users.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Thus, clause 8 makes it an offence for importers to allow non-compliant devices they have imported to be used for purposes other than what had been allowed under the import approval or to fail to comply with a condition specified in the import approval.

sections.label: Forfeiture of dangerous devices
sections.summary: The Bill amends the AMA and RTA to let LTA immediately forfeit dangerous devices and dispose of them after a 30-day notice.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: To mitigate safety hazards arising from the storage of such seized devices, this Bill amends the AMA and the RTA to allow LTA to immediately forfeit devices that LTA has assessed to be dangerous, prior to composition or conviction and to dispose of them after providing a 30-day notice period for objections to be submitted.

sections.label: Active Mobility Bill public paths
sections.summary: The Active Mobility Bill expands the public path network by allowing path-connected open spaces to be declared public paths.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Lastly, to improve clarity of rules for all path users, the Active Mobility Bill expands the public path network by allowing path-connected open spaces to be declared as public paths.

sections.label: Small Motorised Vehicles Bill amendments
sections.summary: Clauses 29, 30 and 31 of the Small Motorised Vehicles Bill amend the Land Transport Authority of Singapore Act, Rapid Transit Systems Act and Road Traffic Act to channel certain LTA-collected sums into the Consolidated Fund.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Lastly, clauses 29, 30 and 31 of the Small Motorised Vehicles Bill makes miscellaneous amendments to the Land Transport Authority of Singapore Act, Rapid Transit Systems Act and the Road Traffic Act to channel certain sums collected by LTA into the Consolidated Fund.

sections.label: Active mobility devices commuting option
sections.summary: Active mobility devices can be an affordable, environmentally-friendly and convenient commuting option when used safely with appropriate regulations and infrastructure, and cycling path infrastructure and the regulatory framework are being improved.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: When used safely, with the appropriate regulations and infrastructure, active mobility devices can be an affordable, environmentally-friendly and convenient commuting option.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: This is why, even as we are heartened by the significant improvement in footpath safety since the use of e-scooters was banned on footpaths from November last year, we are pressing on to improve our cycling path infrastructure and to further strengthen our regulatory framework.

sections.label: Small Motorised Vehicles Safety Bill import
sections.summary: The Small Motorised Vehicles (Safety) Bill controls the import and use of non-compliant devices, which are often a fire risk, and a question is asked on how it will regulate online-bought active mobility devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: But despite these measures, the number of fires involving non-compliant devices continue to remain an issue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Therefore, the introduction of the Small Motorised Vehicles (Safety) Bill is timely as it serves to control the import and use of non-compliant devices, which are often a fire risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: First, I would like to ask how will the Bill regulate the import of active mobility devices that are bought online.

sections.label: Import of replacement parts
sections.summary: A question is asked whether the import of replacement parts, vital for servicing and repairs, will also be regulated under the Bill covering unassembled active mobility devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As the Bill also covers the import of unassembled active mobility devices, I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State whether the import of replacement parts, which are vital for servicing and repairs, will also be regulated.

sections.label: Third-party liability insurance PMDs
sections.summary: The Ministry accepted the Active Mobility Advisory Panel's recommendations in December 2019 to make third-party liability insurance compulsory for PMDs used in the course of work, and a view is expressed that this should extend to all PMD users.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Ministry had, in December 2019, accepted the recommendations made by the Active Mobility Advisory Panel, to make third-party liability insurance compulsory for those who use PMDs in the course of their work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, in my view, this requirement should be extended to all PMD users, as there remains a sizeable number of PMD riders who use PMDs for non-work purposes.

sections.label: Residents evacuated, PMD charging overnight
sections.summary: About 100 residents were evacuated and an SCDF report said a PMD was left to be charged overnight.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: About 100 residents had to be evacuated and, according to SCDF report, there was a PMD being left to be charged overnight.

sections.label: Unapproved PMDs banned from roads
sections.summary: Non-compliant devices without approval labels are not allowed on the road from 1 July onwards.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For those without approval labels, non-compliant, they are not allowed to use on the road from 1 July onwards.

sections.label: Amendments cover path-connected open spaces
sections.summary: Amendments to the Active Mobility Bill extend public path coverage to path-connected open spaces so enforcement can act against rule-flouters there.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Yet, others take advantage of the fact that these places are not visually distinguishable from the public path network and continue zooming through on their devices.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, I am glad that the amendments to the Active Mobility Bill will extend coverage of public paths to include the path-connected open spaces, so that law enforcement can be taken against those who flout the rules in these spaces.

sections.label: Shared responsibility and safety amendments
sections.summary: The amendments are necessary to protect the lives and safety of pedestrians and PMD riders, with everyone sharing responsibility for safety.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This does not only apply to just staying safe from PMDs, but in any situation, everybody has a shared responsibility for staying safe in their environment.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: These amendments are necessary to protect the lives and safety of both pedestrians and the PMD riders.

sections.label: PMD ban in town centre squares
sections.summary: The Bill extends public path coverage to path-connected open spaces, banning PMDs in places such as town centre squares to protect pedestrians.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am also happy to note that this Bill would extend coverage of public paths to include path-connected open spaces.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Therefore, PMDs will also be banned in places, such as town centre squares to protect pedestrians’ safety.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Residents also told me that during the Circuit Breaker period, some PMD riders saw that there were no enforcement officers around, so they feel like what the Chinese say, "the mountain is high and the emperor is far away", and just took the PMDs back on the paths again.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, will the Government use technologies, such as drones and face recognition?

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In terms of pedestrian safety, we must not go backwards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In particular, it is finally introducing a law to make it an offence for a person to import a small motorised vehicle without having a permit to do so.

sections.label: Banning import of non-spec PMDs
sections.summary: The best solution to disallow non-spec e-bikes, e-scooters or other PMDs would simply be to ban its import.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The best solution to disallow non-specs e-bikes, e-scooters or other PMDs would simply be to ban its import.

sections.label: Unauthorised models entering Singapore
sections.summary: Asks how the Government will work with suppliers, retailers, shipping and logistics companies to keep unauthorised models out of Singapore, including from foreign online suppliers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Will the Senior Minister of State share with the House how the Government will work with suppliers and retailers as well as all shipping and logistics companies to ensure that no unauthorised models can be brought into Singapore including from foreign e-commerce online suppliers?

sections.label: Seized vehicles held by LTA
sections.summary: Asks how many vehicles seized under the Act are currently being held by LTA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: On the issue of the disposal of seized vehicles under the Act, may I know currently how many of such seized vehicles are being held by LTA?

sections.label: Food delivery riders' compliance obligations
sections.summary: Recalls a February Parliamentary Question on legal obligations for food delivery companies over riders' compliance, and Minister Khaw Boon Wan's reply on company responsibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In February this year, I asked in a Parliamentary Question whether the Government will consider imposing legal obligations on food delivery companies to ensure that their delivery riders on e-bikes or e-scooters will comply with active mobility or road traffic regulations, including but not limited to compliance with device requirements or proper usage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Minister Khaw Boon Wan said in reply that under the Activity Mobility amendment and the Shared Mobility Enterprises (Control and Licensing) Act, food delivery companies should be responsible for ensuring that their riders ride safely.

sections.label: Action and penalties against delivery companies
sections.summary: Asks whether LTA can and will act against food delivery companies for riders' breaches, and what penalties apply to such companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In lieu of the continuing use of e-scooters by a small number of food delivery riders and their companies not able to stop them, I would like to ask Senior Minister of State Lam to clarify explicitly: (a) besides taking actions against errant riders, can and will LTA take immediate action against their companies to stop such breaches of law?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: (b) What penalties are available against the food delivery companies for failing to ensure their riders' compliance with the law?

sections.label: Return of forfeited non-compliant vehicles
sections.summary: States that a non-compliant vehicle forfeited under new section 51(3) may be returned if LTA receives a written objection showing good cause and no reasonable cause linking it to an offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 53(1A) provides that a non-compliant vehicle forfeited by the LTA under the new section 51(3) may be returned to a person if LTA receives from the person a written objection showing good cause for its return and there is no reasonable cause to believe that the vehicle is linked to an offence.

sections.label: Sale or disposal of non-compliant vehicles
sections.summary: States LTA may sell, destroy or dispose of a non-compliant vehicle if retention is dangerous or raises fire risk, after one month's Gazette notice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 53(3A) provides that LTA may sell, destroy or dispose of a non-compliant vehicle if it is dangerous for the LTA to retain custody or it increases the likelihood of an outbreak of fire at the holding yard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: LTA may do so after giving one month's notice in the Gazette of its intention to do so.

sections.label: One-month notice before disposal
sections.summary: The expedited procedure still requires a one-month notice before LTA may sell, destroy or dispose of a forfeited dangerous vehicle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Even under the expedited procedure introduced by the amendments, there is still a one-month notice period before the LTA can sell, destroy or dispose of a forfeited vehicle that is dangerous or that materially increases the likelihood of an outbreak of fire.

sections.label: Licensing import of small motorised vehicles
sections.summary: The speaker supports a Bill creating a regulatory framework to license imports of small motorised vehicles to promote safety and meet consumer needs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It was a case of market forces running ahead of regulators since we had no laws to ensure that these imported personal mobility devices met safety standards.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I support the intent behind the Bill, which will create a regulatory framework for licensing the import of small motorised vehicles that will promote safety and meet consumer needs.

sections.label: Import regulation restricting competition
sections.summary: Import regulation restricts competition to approved importers and devices, and the Bill's regulations could create entry barriers harming consumers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Import regulation will effectively restrict competition in the market for small motorised vehicles to approved importers and to approved mobility devices.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Overall, the regulations imposed by this Bill could create barriers to entry, which would harm consumers.

sections.label: LTA considering competitive conduct in licensing
sections.summary: The question asks whether LTA can regulate or consider competitive conduct as a factor in licensing importers under the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will LTA be able to regulate or to consider competitive conduct as a factor in licensing importers under this Bill?

sections.label: Forfeiture of non-compliant vehicles
sections.summary: It is proposed to allow the Authority to order forfeiture of non-compliant vehicles if it views storing them as dangerous.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, it is proposed to allow the Authority to order forfeiture of non-compliant vehicles if it is of the view there is a danger in storing them.

sections.label: Releasing vehicles to third-party claimants
sections.summary: Under clause 15(4) of SMVB and proposed section 51(4) of the AMA, the Authority may release a non-compliant vehicle to a third party claiming ownership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Next, under clause 15(4) of SMVB and the proposed section 51(4) of the AMA, the Authority will be vested with the power to release to a third party who claims to be the owner of a non-compliant vehicle even though it was used in a commission of an offence under SMVB and AMA.

sections.label: Footpaths Order void deck exclusion
sections.summary: The Active Mobility (Footpaths) Order 2018 excludes void decks and commercial premises frontage as footpaths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Under the Active Mobility (Footpaths) Order 2018, void decks and the frontage abutting any commercial premises are excluded as footpaths.

sections.label: Town Councils PMD by-laws
sections.summary: Past collisions with PMD users in void decks led 15 Town Councils to enact by-laws banning PMDs there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: We, in this House, are aware of incidents in the past involving people colliding with PMD users in void decks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This has led to 15 Town Councils to enact by-laws to ban use of PMDs at void decks.

sections.label: Banning import of non-compliant PMDs
sections.summary: Banning the import of non-compliant PMDs is a concrete step to stem their inflow into the country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The first line of defence is to stem the inflow of non-compliant PMDs into the country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Hence, banning the import of such devices is a concrete step.

sections.label: Validity period for approved devices
sections.summary: The member asks if MOT sees a need for a validity period for approved devices, as functionality may deteriorate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We also cannot rule out the possibility that some people might do illegal modifications on their devices, compromising the safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Hence, can I ask the Minister if MOT sees the need to have a validity period for the approved devices, as the functionality and reliability of these devices may deteriorate over time?

sections.label: LTA action against delivery companies
sections.summary: The member asks whether LTA will take delivery companies to task if their delivery people use unapproved devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Can I also ask whether LTA will take the delivery companies to task if their delivery people use devices that are not approved?

sections.label: Enforcement and non-compliant device cases
sections.summary: The member asks how the Ministry can enforce regulations when users do not register devices, and how many non-compliant cases were picked up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I would also like to know how the Ministry can enforce these regulations when users do not send their devices for registration and checks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So far, how many cases of non-compliant devices have been picked up?

sections.label: PMD fire import controls
sections.summary: Fires from PMD and PAB charging and explosions doubled, killing one, and the Member asks whether spare parts like battery packs fall under new import controls.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Last year, the number of fires related to charging and explosions of PMDs and PABs also doubled, causing property destruction, injuring inhabitants and even killing one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Many residents have very valid concerns about the situation and I am glad the Minister has plans to tackle it with the establishment of an import controls regime to prevent the import of non-compliant and unsafe devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: These are questions that were raised by previous Members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But I would like to ask whether spare parts, such as battery packs, wheel set-ups, attachments, amongst others, be covered under the new import controls regime?

sections.label: Approved PMDs and import levies
sections.summary: The Member says a wide range of approved PMDs should be provided and asks whether the new import regime will incur resources and raise import levies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It is also prudent to provide a wide range of approved PMDs, including highly affordable models and for a range of uses, from leisure to those for heavier, prolonged use by delivery riders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: That said, will the implementation of the new import regime incur resources and will this lead to increased import levies and so on?

sections.label: Bills on device specifications
sections.summary: The Bills ensure PMDs and PABs meet pre-set specifications to minimise fire and accident risks, and state which devices are permitted on which paths.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Bills will ensure that motorised personal mobility devices (PMDs) and power-assisted bicycles (PABs) meet the pre-set specifications to minimise fire risks and lower risks of accidents on pathways.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I am glad that it is more clearly stated now which mobility devices are permitted on which paths, thus retaining connectivity for non-motorised PMDs and cyclists while limiting the motorised vehicles to certain paths.

sections.label: Dismount near gathering venues
sections.summary: The Member suggests regulations requiring cyclists and non-motorised PMD riders to dismount and push near playgrounds, exercise corners and gathering venues.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   	I suggest that the Minister should consider setting up regulations requiring cyclists and riders of non-motorised PMDs to dismount and push their vehicles when they are near playgrounds, exercise corners and any venues where people gather.

sections.label: Tailored communications on riding areas
sections.summary: The Member says the Ministry must tailor communications to different user groups about where they can and cannot ride to prevent disputes and misunderstandings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: (In English): Second, it is essential for the Ministry to tailor its communications strategies and methods to different groups of users about where they can and cannot ride to prevent disputes and misunderstandings.

sections.label: PMD and PAB fire figures
sections.summary: In 2019 PMD fires, mostly during charging, hit a record 102 cases with 13 other PAB-related fires, about one fire every three days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Safety standards of PMDs and PABs came under scrutiny in 2019 as the number of PMDs catching fire, mostly during charging, had surged to a record high of 102 cases and there were 13 other fires related to PABs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These figures essentially translated into approximately one fire every three days.

sections.label: New path-connected open spaces definition
sections.summary: The Bill defines path-connected open spaces so authorities can designate surfaced, unenclosed, levelled spaces as pedestrian-only, footpaths or shared paths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces a new definition of "path-connected open spaces" that enable the authorities to designate substantially-levelled and unenclosed open spaces that are surfaced, such as courtyards, plazas and atriums, as pedestrian-only paths, footpaths or shared paths.

sections.label: Redesigning spaces and PMD fire causes
sections.summary: The speaker urges authorities to work with property owners on redesigning spaces and cites fire reports saying most PMD and PAB fires come from illegally modified units.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I would thus urge the relevant authorities to work closely with property owners to identify how they can redesign their spaces so that their spaces continue to remain accessible to users, while still being safe for pedestrians and consumers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I do have some other areas of concerns, Mr Speaker, quoting fire investigation reports, which suggest that most PMD and PAB fires are caused by illegally modified units, especially those units that have modified battery compartments.

sections.label: Modified vehicles fire hazards enforcement
sections.summary: A resident's modified vehicles endangered users and created fire hazards; the speaker urges strong enforcement against owners and unauthorised modification providers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Not only did the vehicles he modified endanger the lives of users, he also created potential fire hazards for his own family and immediate neighbours as his home and the public corridor were cluttered with tools of his trade like spare parts, battery compartments and wires.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I had worked with the various agencies like LTA, Town Council, HDB and our grassroots leaders to try and address this issue but we were not quite clear about what guidelines with regard to legislation we could use to effect any change on the resident.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The resident has since moved out but I believe problems like this might exist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, if these modified vehicles are indeed the main culprits of fire, then I urge the Government to take strong enforcement actions against owners of such vehicles and individuals or businesses that provide unauthorised modification services.

sections.label: LTA approval for PMD imports
sections.summary: All fully-assembled motorised PMDs and PABs will need LTA's approval for import.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: All fully-assembled motorised PMDs and PABs will need LTA's approval for import.

sections.label: Import controls may extend later
sections.summary: The Bill applies to fully assembled PMDs and PABs, with possible extension of import controls to partially or completely unassembled vehicles after monitoring.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: For a start, we will apply the Small Motorised Vehicles (Safety) Bill to fully assembled PMDs and PABs, but may, after monitoring the situation, extend import controls to cover partially assembled or completely unassembled vehicles, if necessary.

sections.label: New regulatory framework and held devices
sections.summary: A new piece of the regulatory framework is in place, and over 1,500 non-compliant devices are held in LTA's holding yards.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: We have now, therefore, put in place this new piece in our regulatory framework.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: There are currently more than 1,500 non-compliant devices held in LTA's holding yards.

sections.label: 30-day objection period for disposal
sections.summary: LTA must allow a reasonable 30-day period for objections before disposing of a device.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: LTA is required to provide a reasonable 30-day period for objections to be submitted before the disposal of the device.

sections.label: Dangerous vehicles forfeiture without 30 days
sections.summary: For dangerous vehicles or things, LTA need not wait 30 days before forfeiture, unlike clause 6(b).

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: The only difference with clause 6(b) of the Active Mobility (Amendment No. 2) Bill is that, for dangerous vehicles or things, LTA will not have to wait out for 30 days before forfeiture.

sections.label: 2019 non-compliant PMD enforcement
sections.summary: In 2019, LTA detected 972 users riding non-compliant PMDs and PABs and seized, forfeited and disposed of their devices.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: As I have mentioned earlier, in 2019 alone, LTA detected a total of 972 users riding non-compliant PMDs and PABs, and seized, forfeited and disposed of their devices.

sections.label: Mobile CCTV hotspot trial
sections.summary: LTA launched an 18-month trial of mobile closed-circuit televisions at hotspots to better detect offences such as speeding.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: LTA has launched an 18-month trial of mobile closed-circuit televisions at hotspots to better detect offences, such as speeding.

sections.label: AMP volunteers as of May 2020
sections.summary: As of May 2020, there are over 1,000 AMP volunteers across 73 teams.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: As of May 2020, we have over 1,000 AMP volunteers across 73 teams.

sections.label: Minimum age for e-scooter riders
sections.summary: Amendments were recently passed requiring riders to be at least 16 years old to ride an e-scooter without supervision.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: On the observation that young riders have been committing active mobility offences, we recently passed amendments to require riders to be at least 16 years old to ride an e-scooter without supervision.

sections.label: Third-party liability insurance for device users
sections.summary: The AMAP will study extending third-party liability insurance requirements to individual device users, as raised by Mr Melvin Yong.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Another area of focus for the AMAP this year is to study extending third-party liability insurance requirements to individual device users, as Mr Melvin Yong has spoken about.

sections.label: Active mobility infrastructure and cycling paths
sections.summary: Despite the PMD population right-sizing after the November 2019 footpath prohibition, more active mobility infrastructure is being provided, extending the cycling path network to 1,320 km by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Even though the PMD population has right-sized following the November 2019 footpath prohibition, we are nonetheless pressing on with the provision of more active mobility infrastructure, extending the cycling path network to 1,320 km by 2030 as I had shared with this House in March 2020.
